RagShortTexts: Poliudie names ancestral Rus tribute circuits.
Hosting a collecting retinue consumes local grain and livestock.

Variants.Content: Poliudie names the tribute circuits of ancestral Rus princes and their retinues. Gifts and hospitality linked ruler and locality. Current demands require knowing claimant, grounds and delivery point: princely dues and khanly demands can reach the same household.
A collecting escort guards goods and animals and controls its own consumption. Every extra night burdens hosts; goods collected but not delivered create disputes at accounting.
Invoking ancestral tribute is easier than defining present authority. Clear demands and witnesses preserve revenue better than several retinues collecting the same obligation repeatedly.
Households distinguish local dues from khanly demands and need witnesses to prior payment. Repeated hospitality consumes seed stores and spreads disputes over shortfalls among neighbors.
